title: Reverse-Seared Ribeye for the Crew
seoTitle: Reverse-Seared Ribeye for the Crew | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Steakhouse crust with smoker depth—ten ribeyes, one plan
subtitle: Smoked then seared boneless ribeyes, compound butter, for ten
description: Adapted from classic reverse-sear technique (Meat Church, Hey Grill Hey): boneless ribeyes smoke low at 225°F to 115°F, rest, then sear hard to 130°F medium-rare with garlic-herb compound butter.

steps.title: Season the ribeyes
steps.instruction: Pat steaks dry. Coat with oil, then salt, pepper, paprika, and garlic powder on all sides. Rest 20 minutes at room temp.

steps.title: Smoke low at 225°F
steps.instruction: Smoke steaks at 225°F until internal temp reaches 115°F for medium-rare, about 35–45 minutes.

steps.title: Compound butter
steps.instruction: Mix softened butter, rosemary, and minced garlic. Roll into a log or keep soft for finishing.

steps.title: Sear hard
steps.instruction: Sear in screaming-hot cast iron or over grill at 500°F+ 90 seconds per side until crust forms and internal hits 130°F medium-rare.

steps.title: Butter baste
steps.instruction: Add compound butter to pan off direct flame; tilt and baste steaks 30 seconds. Rest 5 minutes tented with foil.

steps.title: Hold at 170°F
steps.instruction: If holding, tent with foil and place in 170°F oven up to 20 minutes. Do not exceed 145°F internal on the line.

steps.title: Tonight's board
steps.instruction: Steaks on a board with extra compound butter melting on top. Call temps: 130°F medium-rare pull.

steps.title: Leftovers
steps.instruction: Slice cold for steak sandwiches with horseradish mayo. Reheat gently in au jus—don't re-sear.

proTips: 115°F off the smoker + hard sear lands medium-rare—adjust to 120°F for medium.
Dry surface = better crust; pat again before searing.
Don't skip the rest or juices run when you cut on the line.
tonightSpread: Ribeyes on a board with compound butter.
leftovers: Slice over a wedge salad with blue cheese.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Reverse sear gives even edge-to-edge pink and a real crust. Steaks hold tented at 170°F up to 20 minutes without overcooking if pulled right.
mealPrepNotes: Season early. Smoke in batches if smoker space is tight. Sear to order if possible; otherwise hold tented at 170°F max 20 minutes.
